newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees copper exports at avg $0.90/lb next year.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees copper exports at avg $0.90/lb next year.

text.p: Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress Wednesday the government's budget estimated an average price for the country's copper exports next year of $0.90 per pound.
He said the government's estimate for the average price of its copper exports this year was $1.00 per pound, compared to an average of $1.30 last year.
"If the prices of our exports had kept their level on international markets, our traditional exports for 1997 would have been $250 million higher than we are estimating," Camet said.

The government expects traditional exports next year will value $4.1 billion and will account for the majority of an estimated two percent increase in the value of total exports, which were estimated at $6.05 billion, Camet said.
"The substantial increase in traditional exports will more than compensate for the price fall in our principal exports - particularly in copper," Camet said.
Peru is the world's sixth largest copper producer. The country's largest producer, Southern Peru Copper Corp, accounts for around 60 percent of the country's output.
Production rose 22.3 percent to 274,712 tonnes in the first seven months of the year compared with the same period last year, according to latest figures from the Energy and Mines Ministry.
In 1995, copper output rose 10.8 percent to 404,990 tonnes from 365,513 tonnes in 1994.
